newsitem.title: USA: Nabisco net falls but operations stronger after restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Nabisco net falls but operations stronger after restructuring.

text.p: Nabisco Holdings Corp. Monday reported lower quarterly and annual net profits but stronger operating results as the company's snacks and food businesses improved after a costly restructuring.
"Through our restructuring and renewed focus on core brands, we significantly improved our performance and strengthened the company," said H. John Greeniaus, chairman and chief executive.

The holding company for Nabisco Inc. said profits fell to $110 million, or 41 cents a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $116 million, or 44 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales edged up to $2.48 billion from $2.35 billion.
Full-year earnings plunged to $17 million, or 6 cents a share, from $295 million, or $1.13 a share, in 1995. Sales rose 7 percent to $8.89 billion from $8.29 billion.
The results include restructuring charges of $70 million in the fourth quarter and $525 million for full-year 1996.

Excluding the one-time charges, Nabisco's fourth-quarter income shot up 30 percent to $151 million, or 56 cents a share, from $116 million, or 44 cents a share, a year earlier. Nabisco said the increase was due mainly to the strength of its domestic business, which benefited from renewed focus on core brands and the impact of restructuring savings.

For full-year 1996, operating income rose 19 percent to $374 million, or $1.40 a share, from $314 million, or $1.20 a share, in 1995, led by a strong rebound in the domestic biscuit business in the second half of the year.

"We're particularly pleased with results of our Biscuit Co., which in the second-half achieved excellent earnings growth while making fundamental changes in its structure and strategies," said Greeniaus. "Planters nuts, Life Savers candies and our margarines were also very strong contributors."
Nabisco's brands also include Oreo, SnackWell's, Ritz, Chips Ahoy!, A.1., Grey Poupon, Parkay and Fleischmann's.

However, Nabisco said international profits, which had grown more quickly than the company's overall performance for several years, fell amid difficult economic conditions in several countries, higher commodity prices and slower progress with the integration of several recent acquisitions.
"To date, we have fully realised our projected savings, which are targeted to reach a pre-tax level of $200 million a year in 1998 and beyond," Greeniaus said.

"The bulk of these savings will be invested in marketing and product development programmes that will drive our future growth. In all, the organisational changes and momentum of 1996 set the stage for solid gains in 1997."
Parsippany, N.J.-based Nabisco's stock edge up 12.5 cents to $39.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
